context_pill: Direct Tax | Diversion vs Application of Income
example_summary: XYZ Ltd. acquired a sole-proprietorship business via a sale deed with a condition to pay ₹ 15,000 p.a. to the seller's wife, creating an overriding charge diverted at source.
source_provision:
### Statutory Comparison: Diversion vs Application of Income

| Feature / Parameter | Diversion of Income by Overriding Title | Application of Income |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Timing of Obligation** | Pre-existing obligation attached to the source before income reaches the assessee. | Post-receipt obligation arising after income accrues or reaches the assessee. |
| **Nature of Charge** | Overriding charge creating a paramount legal title in favor of a third party. | Voluntary or contractual allocation of income already earned. |
| **Flow of Revenue** | Direct diversion at source; income never becomes part of assessee's income. | Income reaches the assessee first and is subsequently spent or transferred. |
| **Tax Treatment** | Entirely **excluded** from the Total Income of the assessee. | Fully **included** in Total Income; taxable without deduction unless specifically allowed. |

### Key Statutory & Judicial Tests

* **Supreme Court Test (CIT v. Sitaldas Tirathdas)**: Is the obligation attached to the source of income itself, compelling the assessee to apply it for another's benefit?
* **Enforceable Paramount Title**: The third party must possess an independent, legal, enforceable right over the source or net revenue.
* **Encumbered Purchase of Asset**: When an asset or going concern is purchased subject to a mandatory charge in the sale deed, the charge is attached to the source.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Judicial Benchmark**: Where an obligation is created as an integral condition of acquiring an income-generating asset, the revenue diverted to discharge that obligation represents a **Diversion of Income by Overriding Title**, not an application of profit.
